notes: Frames with a gradient or image background no longer flatten into one image. The background arrives as a picture of just the background, and everything on top stays editable.
The same goes for frames inside frames, and for frame strokes with a gradient or a different width on each side.
A frame still flattens if its background is a video or an image with adjustments (exposure, contrast and so on). The report says so.
testFocus: Send the Meta social frames again: the background should be one image layer called Background, with shapes, text and images on top as separate layers.
Turn on the Figma Reference layer and check the background matches: gradient direction and colours, and image fills cropped and positioned like Figma.
If you have them, try angular and diamond gradients, and an image fill set to Fit, Crop or Tile, or rotated.
